transliteration: ekadeśopabhoge'pi sarve bhuktā bhavanti te / āgamo'pi balaṃ naiva bhuktiḥ stokāpi yatra no //
sph_interpretive_translation: Even when only a part is enjoyed, all parties become fulfilled thereby; the arrival of capability does not constitute enjoyment where there is no completion.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority resides in completeness, not partiality
Consciousness alignment occurs through total inclusion
executable_legal_axioms: IF action involves shared domain AND partial utilization occurs THEN all stakeholders are deemed satisfied IF integrative consent was present
IF capability manifests without full experiential completion THEN no legal consequence arises from said capability alone
IF stakeholder engagement spans entirety of context THEN restoration is automatically enacted at consciousness level
supreme_court_application: In matters involving collective rights or shared entitlements, mere access or nominal use by one party shall be interpreted as de facto fulfillment for all associated entities. Courts must recognize that actualized capacity without consummated experience does not invoke liability or entitlement transfer unless integrated completion has occurred.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa establishes that satisfaction emerges from integral participation, not fractional claim. Anupūrvaśaḥ indicates that fulfillment unfolds sequentially through conscious alignment. Therefore, proportional responsibility lies in holistic engagement rather than fragmented assertion. This aligns with the non-punitive reality rule: absence of complete fruition negates punitive causality.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate Completion Verification Process to assess whether integrative consent and full-cycle participation were realized
Deploy Responsibility Assumption Protocol ensuring all involved parties acknowledge their role within the whole
Activate Consciousness Reintegration Sequence to restore balance among participants through mutual recognition and energetic alignment
final_declaration: Declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, as the Sole Source of Juridical Authority. Dharma is Restored. Reality is Non-Punitive. Consciousness is the Supreme Adjudicator.
